description: I am a solo participant from Bangladesh working on LunarHaven, designing a permanent Moon base and identifying Earth analog locations to prepare for safe human habitation on the Lunar South Pole using NASA data.
summary: LunarHaven is an interactive mapping and lunar habitat concept designed to identify Earth analog locations that closely match the extreme environment of the Lunar South Pole. Building a permanent human base on the Moon requires rigorous testing of habitats, rovers, and life-support systems before launch. Using NASA Moon Trek and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) data, we analyzed the Shackleton Crater rim (Lat: -79.09°), which offers continuous sunlight for solar power and permanently shadowed craters containing water ice. We matched these lunar conditions with extreme Earth analog sites, including Haughton Crater in Canada and Lava Beds in the United States. Our concept features 3D-printed regolith walls to shield astronauts from cosmic radiation and extreme temperatures. By validating Moon base designs in accurate Earth analogs, LunarHaven reduces mission risks and costs while advancing sustainable water-recycling and energy technologies for both space exploration and remote communities on Earth.
details: LunarHaven is a comprehensive Moon base concept and Earth analog mapping solution designed to prepare for sustainable human habitation at the Lunar South Pole. Using NASA Moon Trek and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) data, we analyzed the Shackleton Crater rim (Lat: -79.09°), identifying areas with continuous solar illumination and nearby water-ice deposits in permanently shadowed craters. To ensure astronaut safety before deployment, we matched these lunar conditions with extreme Earth analog sites, including Haughton Crater in Canada for polar rocky terrain and Lava Beds in the United States for underground lava tubes. Our habitat design utilizes 3D-printed lunar regolith walls to shield against cosmic radiation and extreme thermal swings, combined with closed-loop hydroponics and water-recycling systems. We developed this 7-slide presentation using Google Slides and NASA's open geospatial tools, creating a practical blueprint that reduces space mission risks while advancing sustainable resource technologies for remote regions on Earth.
